summary: Source decomposition of the deduction 'Serre's conjecture in the case eps = 1, k = 2 implies modularity of elliptic curves over Q', following Serre's own section 4.6 (Theoreme 4 and Lemme 5) with its inputs: the weight-two-iff-finite-flat criterion of his 2.8, the replacement of absolute irreducibility by irreducibility over F_p at odd p from his 3.3, the eigenvalue lifting of Deligne-Serre, the pigeonhole over the finite set of weight-2 level-N newforms, the algebraic-integer norm argument giving exact equality of coefficients, and Faltings' isogeny theorem in the form of his Korollar 2. Carayol's corollary supplies the exact conductor and the equality of L-functions. Not covered: the construction of the modular parametrisation X_0(N) -> E itself (Serre concludes only 'quotient of J_0(N)'), Mazur's rational-isogeny theorem, and the bad coefficients.

nodes.title: Lemme 5 of the source: for all but finitely many p, E[p] is irreducible and has conductor exactly N
nodes.statement: Let E be an elliptic curve over Q with conductor N and modular invariant j_E, and for each prime p let rho_p: G_Q -> GL_2(F_p) be the representation on the p-division points. Then det rho_p = chi, the mod p cyclotomic character. There is a constant C_E such that for every p > C_E: (4.6.2) rho_p is irreducible, and (4.6.3) the conductor of rho_p equals N. Quantitatively: by Mazur's theorem (4.6.2) holds as soon as p > 163; the definition of the conductor of E in terms of l-adic representations shows the conductor N_p of rho_p always DIVIDES N (which the source notes would already suffice for the argument); and for p > 5 one has N_p = N if and only if (a) p does not divide N and (b) for every l with v_l(N) = 1, p does not divide v_l(j_E). Note that v_l(N) = 1 means E has multiplicative reduction at l, so v_l(j_E) < 0.
hypotheses: E is an elliptic curve over Q; no semistability is assumed here (unlike in the source's Proposition 5)
the bound p > 163 for irreducibility is Mazur's theorem on rational isogenies of prime degree, quoted and not proved in the source
condition (b) is a finite condition because only the finitely many l with v_l(N) = 1 occur, and for each of those v_l(j_E) is a fixed nonzero integer
the criterion N_p = N is stated for p > 5
Reviewer: (4.6.2) is irreducibility over F_p; the upgrade to absolute irreducibility needed by (3.3.1_?) is the separate bracketed remark of 3.3, valid for p different from 2 (next node)
proofSteps: det rho_p = chi is (4.6.1), stated without justification in the source; the Weil pairing on E[p] is the standard reason (reviewer gloss, not in the source).
Irreducibility for p > 163 is Mazur's theorem; the source calls the whole of Lemme 5 'un resultat connu'.
That N_p divides N follows from the definition of the conductor of E via l-adic representations (the source cites SGA 7, Ogg, Serre-Tate).

The equality criterion (a)-(b) is given in the source only as 'on verifie que', with no proof. Reviewer correction of the drafted justification, which invoked Proposition 5 and v_p(j_E): Proposition 5 computes the weight k at p for a semistable curve over Q_p and says nothing about ramification at a prime l different from p. The relevant computation is the Tate curve at l with v_l(N) = 1: rho_p is unramified at l if and only if p divides v_l(q_E) = -v_l(j_E), so condition (b) is on v_l(j_E). Condition (a) is needed because N_p is prime to p by definition. The restriction p > 5 presumably handles the additive places (reviewer reading; the source gives no reason).
acceptance: Check the criterion on a semistable curve with a prime l of multiplicative reduction and p dividing v_l(j_E), confirming that N_p is then a proper divisor of N
Check that for odd p irreducibility over F_p upgrades to absolute irreducibility using oddness, as in the source's 3.3 bracket (b')

nodes.title: For p different from 2, irreducibility over F_p implies absolute irreducibility
nodes.statement: Suppose rho: G_Q -> GL_2(F_p) satisfies det rho = chi and p is different from 2. Then irreducibility of rho over F_p implies absolute irreducibility, i.e. irreducibility over F_p-bar. Reason: det rho = chi is odd, so the eigenvalues of rho(c) for c complex conjugation are +1 and -1, and since p is different from 2 these are distinct; if rho became a direct sum of two one-dimensional representations over F_p-bar, that decomposition would have to be the one given by the eigenvectors of rho(c), hence would be rational over F_p, contradicting irreducibility over F_p.
hypotheses: p different from 2 is essential: at p = 2 the two eigenvalues of rho(c) coincide and the argument fails
det rho = chi (or more generally det rho odd) is what makes rho(c) have eigenvalues +1 and -1
the argument is about a 2-dimensional representation; it does not generalize to higher rank

Reviewer: the source treats only a decomposition of rho over F_p-bar into a DIRECT SUM of two characters. The non-split case reduces to it: if a line L over F_p-bar is stable and some Galois conjugate L' of L differs from L, then rho = L + L' is a direct sum; otherwise L is defined over F_p, contradicting (b'). This step is implicit in the source
proofSteps: The source states the argument in a bracketed remark in 3.3, replacing hypothesis (b) (absolute irreducibility) by the apparently weaker (b') (irreducibility over F_p) when p is different from 2.
acceptance: Check at p = 2 that the implication fails, by exhibiting an F_2-irreducible representation that becomes reducible over F_4
Check that the eigenvector decomposition of rho(c) is defined over F_p when the eigenvalues are distinct and lie in F_p

Si alors p se décomposait sur Fp en somme directe de deux représentations de dimension 1, cette décomposition ne pourrait être que celle donnée par les vecteurs propres de p (c ), donc serait rationnelle sur Fp , ce qui contredirait (b') .

nodes.title: Why the Serre data of E[p] is (N, 2, trivial): good reduction gives finiteness at p and determinant chi
nodes.statement: For p not dividing N, E has good reduction at p, so rho_p is finite at p in the sense of the source's 2.8, and det rho_p = chi. Hence by the source's 1.3 the nebentypus eps is trivial, and by Proposition 4 of 2.8 the Serre weight is k = 2. The conjecture (3.2.4?) then specializes to (3.3.1?): there is a cusp form f of weight 2 and level N with coefficients in F_p-bar which is a normalized Hecke eigenform with rho_f isomorphic to rho_p; by (3.2.6?) - itself a conjecture of the source, marked with the subscript '?' like (3.2.4?) and (3.3.1?) - this form has coefficients in F_p except possibly when rho_p is unramified at p, which can happen only if p = 2. Equivalently (3.3.2?): rho_p occurs as a Jordan-Holder quotient of the representation of G_Q on the p-division points of J_0(N).
hypotheses: p must not divide N for the good-reduction argument; the excluded primes are among the finitely many of Lemme 5

the identification k = 2 is Proposition 4 of 2.8. In case (ii) its proof is written only for p different from 2; the source says the case p = 2 'est un peu different, mais se traite de facon analogue' without giving it, and the uniqueness of the finite flat prolongation it cites ([35], prop. 3.3.2) needs e < p-1. At p = 2 this step therefore inherits the boundary recorded in this job's AlgebraicModularFormsAndSerreWeights packet

the coefficient field is F_p-bar in general; F_p-rationality is a separate assertion, coming from the conjectural (3.2.6?). The source says it holds 'sauf peut-etre' in the unramified-at-p case, which needs p = 2; it does not assert that rationality fails there (reviewer correction of 'can fail exactly')
the level in (3.3.1?) is the prime-to-p Artin conductor N(rho_p), which by Lemme 5 equals N only for p outside the finite exceptional set
proofSteps: E has good reduction at p, so E[p] extends to a finite flat group scheme over Z_p, i.e. rho_p is finite at p.
det rho_p = chi gives eps = 1 by 1.3 and k = 2 mod (p-1) by Proposition 2; Proposition 4 then upgrades this to k = 2 exactly.
Serre's 3.3 assembles these into the statements (3.3.1?) and (3.3.2?).
acceptance: Check that the finite flat model of E[p] at p is the p-torsion of the Neron model, and that this is what 'finite at p' means in 2.8

Check which primes must be excluded. Reviewer correction: in Serre's route the exclusions are those of Lemme 5 (p > C_E, which includes p not dividing N); the nebentypus is trivial directly from det rho_p = chi by 1.3, so the atlas stage's exclusion of primes dividing phi(N_E) does not arise. nodes.title: Pigeonhole on a finite set of newforms, and the norm argument giving exact equality of coefficients
nodes.statement: For each p > C_E, (3.3.1?) gives a mod p eigenform f_p of weight 2 and level N. By (3.1.6) - which is Deligne-Serre's eigenvalue lifting lemma - f_p lifts to a normalized characteristic-zero cuspidal Hecke eigenform F = sum A_n q^n of weight 2 and level N with algebraic integer coefficients whose reduction is f_p. A priori F depends on p; but the weight and level are fixed, so only finitely many F are possible, whence there is a single F with F-bar = f_p for all p in an INFINITE set P of primes. For l a prime not dividing N, E has good reduction at l; let a_l be the trace of the corresponding Frobenius endomorphism. Then a_l = a_{l,p} mod p for every p different from l, so the algebraic integer A_l - a_l has zero image in F_p-bar for every p in P with p different from l; since P is infinite, A_l = a_l for every l not dividing N. In particular the A_l lie in Z.
hypotheses: the pigeonhole step needs the space of weight-2 level-N cusp forms to be finite-dimensional, so that only finitely many normalized eigenforms occur
the lifting (3.1.6) produces a form with coefficients in the ring of integers of a number field; the source states 'a coefficients dans Z-bar'
the norm argument needs A_l - a_l to be an algebraic integer whose reduction vanishes at infinitely many primes; a nonzero algebraic integer cannot have infinitely many prime divisors of its norm
the conclusion A_l = a_l is asserted for l not dividing N only; the bad coefficients require a separate argument

Reviewer: Serre's passage from 'the A_l for l not dividing N are in Z' to 'they define a Weil curve E_F' uses, without comment, the rationality of the remaining coefficients and the Eichler-Shimura construction of E_F as a quotient of J_0(N); neither is in a source read (see the gaps on bad coefficients and on the modular quotient)
proofSteps: Apply (3.3.1?) for each p > C_E to get f_p, then (3.1.6) to lift to F depending on p.
Finiteness of the set of possible F plus infinitude of the primes gives a single F and an infinite set P.
Congruence a_l = a_{l,p} mod p for p in P and the infinitude of P force A_l = a_l.
The A_l then define a Weil curve E_F of level a divisor of N.
acceptance: Check that the norm argument is applied to A_l - a_l as an algebraic integer, and that its vanishing modulo infinitely many primes is what forces it to be zero
Check that the coefficient field of F is Q, i.e. that K_F = Q, and record how the bad coefficients A_l for l dividing N are pinned down

nodes.title: Faltings' isogeny theorem closes the argument, and Carayol's corollary gives the exact conductor
nodes.statement: Faltings Korollar 2: for abelian varieties A_1, A_2 over a number field K the following are equivalent: (i) A_1 and A_2 are isogenous; (ii) T_l(A_1) tensor Q_l is isomorphic to T_l(A_2) tensor Q_l as a Galois module; (iii) L_v(s, A_1) = L_v(s, A_2) for almost all places v; (iv) the same for all v. The equivalence of (i) and (ii) is Satz 4 (End_K(A) tensor Z_l -> End_{Galois}(T_l(A)) is an isomorphism), that of (ii) and (iii) is Satz 3 (semisimplicity of the Galois action on T_l(A) tensor Q_l) together with Cebotarev. Applying this to E and the curve E_F attached to the newform F, whose l-adic representations agree by the coefficient equality, gives an isogeny over Q, which is the last step of the source's Theoreme 4. For the conductor, Carayol's Corollaire to his Theoreme (A) with F = Q and k = 2 gives directly that for a rational normalized newform f in S_2(Gamma_0(N)) the L-function of the associated elliptic curve E_f equals L(f, s) and the geometric conductor of E_f equals N.
hypotheses: Faltings' results are over an arbitrary number field K; the application here is K = Q
Korollar 2 gives isogeny from agreement of local L-factors at almost all places - the 'almost all' version already suffices

Carayol's conductor statement is a consequence of local-global compatibility at EVERY finite place including the bad ones, together with Ogg's conductor formula; it is not a consequence of agreement of unramified traces alone
Serre's Remarque (2) records that the form F produced in the proof of Theoreme 4 is PRIMITIVE, citing a theorem of Carayol

Placement note (reviewer): the atlas gives the isogeny step to R29.5 ('Use R19's Tate-module identification and R28's isogeny theorem to obtain an isogeny A_f -> E over Q'). R29.4 owns the Galois comparison and the exact conductor. This node holds both; the stage order R29.4 -> R29.5 is respected, but the R29.5 coverage record must not report the isogeny step as unread

Carayol's Corollaire is stated for a rational NEWFORM f in S_2(Gamma_0(N)); its proof identifies the Galois representation of Theoreme (A) with H^1 of E_f by Cebotarev, deduces the L-function equality from Theoreme (A), and gets the conductor equality 'compte tenu du travail de Ogg'. F = Q has odd degree, so the standing even-degree hypothesis of Theoreme (A) does not apply
proofSteps: From (4.6.4) the l-adic representations attached to E and to E_F have the same traces of Frobenius at all good l, hence are isomorphic: by Cebotarev after semisimplification, and semisimplicity is Faltings' Satz 3. Serre states the isomorphism directly without naming these steps; the elaboration is the drafter's and follows Faltings' proof of Korollar 2.
Faltings Korollar 2 (ii) implies (i) gives the isogeny over Q.
Serre then concludes Theoreme 4: E is a Weil curve of level N, and in particular is isomorphic to a quotient of the Jacobian J_0(N) of X_0(N).

The exactness of the level is not spelled out by Serre, who concludes 'D'ou le th. 4' from the isogeny with E_F, a Weil curve of level dividing N. Reviewer reconstruction: E and E_F have the same conductor N, and Carayol's Corollaire (for the newform attached to F; F is primitive by Serre's Remarque (2), citing Carayol) identifies the level with that conductor. The weaker conclusion 'quotient of J_0(N)' needs only that level-M quotients for M dividing N are quotients of J_0(N).
acceptance: Check that the isogeny produced is over Q and not merely over Qbar, which is what Korollar 2 gives since it is stated over K
Check the equality of bad local Euler factors directly, since Korollar 2(iii) is stated for almost all v but (iv) asserts all v

nodes.title: The statement obtained, and what it does not give
nodes.statement: Theoreme 4 of the source: granting (3.3.1?) - the case eps = 1, k = 2 of Serre's conjecture (the drafter adds that it is now a theorem of Khare-Wintenberger and Kisin; that remark is not in the source and is supplied, if at all, by the ClassicalSerreModularity packet) - every elliptic curve E over Q is a Weil curve of level N, its conductor; in particular E is isomorphic to a quotient of the Jacobian J_0(N) of the modular curve X_0(N). The source records that all of its applications except the last use the conjecture only in the case eps = 1, k = 2. The companion Theoreme 5, also conditional on (3.3.1?), extends the conclusion to abelian varieties with real multiplications: every abelian variety X over Q of dimension n with K_X = Q tensor End_Q(X) a totally real number field of degree n is isomorphic to a quotient of J_0(N), where N is the n-th root of the conductor of X - this uses (4.7.1) that X defines a degree-2 system of lambda-adic representations rational over K_X with cyclotomic determinant, and (4.7.2) that the conductor of X is of the form N^n. Nothing about ranks or the Birch-Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture is asserted.
hypotheses: Theoreme 4 is stated conditionally on (3.3.1?); the source is from 1987 and the conjecture was open
the level is the conductor N of E, and the conclusion is 'quotient of J_0(N)', i.e. a modular parametrisation exists but the source does not construct the map X_0(N) -> E explicitly
Theoreme 5 requires K_X to be totally real of degree exactly n = dim X; it is the real-multiplication case, not general GL_2-type over a number field
the source's Remarque (3) gives a further analogous application to Shimura's question over a real quadratic field, again conditional on (3.2.4?)
proofSteps: Theoreme 4 is proved by the chain: Lemme 5, the weight-2 specialization of the conjecture, the eigenvalue lifting, the pigeonhole, the coefficient identity (4.6.4), and Faltings' isogeny theorem.

Theoreme 5's proof is stated to be analogous, recovering Theoreme 4 for n = 1; the source gives only its outline, through (4.7.1)-(4.7.2) and further steps (4.7.3)-(4.7.5), where the irreducibility of rho_p for large p is referred to Faltings ([14], p. 204) or to an elementary argument.
acceptance: Check that the conclusion is a quotient of J_0(N), and that producing a nonconstant morphism X_0(N) -> E requires the Abel-Jacobi map and a choice of rational cusp, which the source does not supply
Check that no rank statement is inferred; the source makes none

review.notes: All 6 nodes and 7 drafted links checked against the library copies of Serre 1987, Faltings 1983, Carayol 1986 and Deligne-Serre 1974 (four SHA-256 hashes re-verified); the catalogue claims in the coverage and gaps (Mazur 1978 absent; Mazur-Swinnerton-Dyer and Diamond-Shurman present; Shimura 1971 unresolved) were confirmed. Verdicts: 2 verified, 4 corrected, 0 unverifiable. Main corrections: (1) the justification of Lemme 5's conductor criterion invoked Proposition 5 and v_p(j_E); Proposition 5 is about the weight at p, the source gives the criterion without proof, and the relevant computation is the Tate curve at l (new gap). (2) (3.2.6?) is itself conjectural (Serre's subscript '?'), and it says F_p-rationality holds except perhaps in the unramified case, not that it fails there. (3) Serre calls Proposition 4 at p = 2 analogous rather than omitting it. (4) The phi(N) exclusion is not part of Serre's route. (5) The isogeny step sits in the R29.4 node although the atlas assigns it to R29.5 (placement note; R29.5 coverage updated). (6) The Khare-Wintenberger-Kisin remark is not from the source. Links: 5 verified, 1 corrected reason (R15.4 -> R29.2: p = 2 wording), 1 annotated (R29.4 -> R29.6: needs R29.5 material); 2 added supplier links (FaltingsFinitenessAndIsogenyTheorems:R28.6 and AutomorphicGaloisRepresentations:R19.4 -> R29.4 node), both with stage texts read and both transitive in the atlas.
